reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, post-fix stale re-review batch 1, 2026-08-02

samples_reviewed.question_text: What is the next number in the pattern: 1, 10, 1, 10, 1, 10?
What is the next number in the pattern: 2, 10, 2, 10, 2, 10?
What is the next number in the pattern: 10, 13, 10, 13, 10, 13?
What is the next number in the pattern: 2, 6, 2, 6, 2, 6?
What is the next number in the pattern: 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1?
What is the missing piece (position 6) in the pattern?
Fill in the chart with the correct counts.
What is the next number in the pattern: 10, 3, 10, 3, 10, 3?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Six of eight samples correctly ask to determine the next term, e.g. "What is the next number in the pattern: 10, 13, 10, 13, 10, 13?", but seed 55's "Fill in the chart with the correct counts." never mentions a pattern, sequence, or next term, so its connection to the competency's verb 'determine the next term' is not evidenced by its text.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Every numeric pattern in the packet is a two-element alternation -- "1, 10, 1, 10, 1, 10" (42), "2, 6, 2, 6, 2, 6" (45), "2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1" (46), "10, 3, 10, 3, 10, 3" (72) -- while the competency's own worked example is a three-letter cycle (a, b, c, a, b, c, a, __, __); no letter-based or 3+-term-cycle pattern appears anywhere.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Prompts stay short and formulaic across the board, e.g. "What is the next number in the pattern: 2, 6, 2, 6, 2, 6?", comfortably within Grade 1 Q3 reading demand.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All six 'next number' items share the identical AB-alternation template with only the two numeral values changed (1&10, 2&10, 10&13, 2&6, 2&1, 10&3), so despite four different formatter shells (mcq, cloze, read_mcq, set_fill_in_blank) the underlying pattern structure never varies.

competency_alignment.rationale: Where the task is legibly posed, the variation (which two values alternate) stays on pattern-continuation, but seed 55's undirected "Fill in the chart with the correct counts." cannot be confirmed from its text to build the repeating-pattern skill rather than a counting or tallying skill.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values used in the patterns (1, 2, 3, 6, 10, 12, 13) stay small and simple, appropriate for a Grade 1 Q3 pattern-recognition task.
